chapters.title: Use cases: code auditing and security

features.name: AL Graph
features.description: A new tool in the AL tools package that constructs call graphs to analyze code structure, identify caller-callee relationships, external integration points, dependencies, and security vulnerabilities.

features.name: AL Graph query language
features.description: A rich query language that allows users to construct complex queries to find callers of specific objects, methods that interact with tables, and trace security boundaries. Queries are documented on MS Learn.
caveats: Users should consult MS Learn documentation for query syntax

features.name: AL Graph DGML export
features.description: Export format for AL Graph queries that produces graph representations suitable for human analysis of call relationships.

features.name: AL Graph SARIF export
features.description: Export format for AL Graph queries in SARIF format, designed to be flat and easily consumable by agents.

features.name: AL Graph meta model extraction
features.description: One-time process to build a meta model representation of caller-callee relationships in an app using the 'extract whole' method. The meta model is stored as JSON and queried multiple times.

features.name: HTTP client caller auditing
features.description: AL Graph query capability to identify all callers to HTTP client and trace the call paths that can reach HTTP requests, useful for auditing external integration points.

features.name: Non-debuggable to debuggable boundary audit
features.description: AL Graph capability to find all callees of non-debuggable methods and identify where secrets could be inadvertently exposed by debugging in debuggable code reached from non-debuggable methods.
caveats: This is a security concern where breakpoints in debuggable methods reached from non-debuggable code can leak information
